newsitem.title: USA: Jobless rate in Wis. hits lowest level since 1970.
newsitem.headline: Jobless rate in Wis. hits lowest level since 1970.

text.p: Wisconsin's unemployment rate in October dropped to 3.1 percent, the lowest level registered in the state since January 1970, according to the state's department of workforce development.
The seasonally adjusted rate for October fell from 3.3 percent in September. Wisconsin's unemployment rate in October 1995 was 3.7 percent.

"Employment opportunities in Wisconsin have been truly phenomenal," said Richard Wegner, acting secretary of the workforce development department in a news release. "We are especially gratified by reports that employers are stepping up to the plate to hire first-time workers leaving the welfare rolls."

In Madison, the state capital, the jobless rate fell to 1.4 percent in October from 1.5 percent in September, making it the lowest rate for that city probably since World War II, according to the release.
